clue.text: Not having enough space, set up a tent across river

indicators.note: the tent-pitching word is laid across the river's letter, so it surrounds it

parts.note: to set up a tent is to camp, past tense camped
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Campers squeezed for room pitch their tent across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramped space is one too small to move about in, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Royal regatta town is intimidating, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelt differently

parts.note: intimidating someone cows them, so cows means intimidating

explanation.surface: A smart sailing venue is described as daunting, or so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: COWES, on the Isle of Wight off England's south coast, hosts Cowes Week, the famous sailing regatta with royal patronage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Wight harbour is home to the Royal Yacht Squadron and the annual sailing week.

clue.text: Emblem of the US representing a cleaner image

indicators.note: representing is read as re-presenting, laying out the letters of the phrase afresh

explanation.surface: A national symbol is said to stand for a cleaner public image.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald bird of prey on the Great Seal is the national symbol of the United States.

clue.text: Spot beer, getting in round

indicators.note: getting in says the round letter goes inside the drink

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer, standing for the drink
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone spots a beer while buying a round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting in round' reads as buying drinks in a pub, but it puts O inside PINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot and a point are both a dot or a particular place, as in a point on a map.

clue.text: Some deride Greek as an academic qualification

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people mock studying Greek as a university subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A university award such as a BA is the standard example of an academic qualification.

clue.text: Load vehicle and set off

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to set off is to go

explanation.surface: Someone loads up the car and drives away.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the freight a ship or plane carries, a load of goods.

clue.text: US city elegantly fashionable in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish, elegantly fashionable
ago means in the past, as in long ago

explanation.surface: An American city that used to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windy City on Lake Michigan is a major American metropolis.

clue.text: Curiously un-libertarian patriotic song

indicators.note: curiously signals that the letters are put together in an odd, rearranged way

explanation.surface: A flag-waving anthem is oddly at odds with liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the song itself proclaims 'Britons never will be slaves'. It is a stirring British anthem sung at the Last Night of the Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: The 18th-century anthem by Thomas Arne celebrates British naval power, a classic patriotic song.

clue.text: Where nurses work so as to make progress

definitions.meaning: nurses work on hospital wards, read as two words

explanation.surface: Nurses work in the wards so that patients can improve.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means forward or ahead, the direction of making progress.

clue.text: Tree exuding badly, splitting half of bark

parts.note: a weeping wound exudes fluid, so weeping means exuding

indicators.note: splitting says the word for badly goes into the middle, cutting the other piece in two
half of takes just one half of the dog's noise, here its second half

parts.note: a dog's bark is bow-wow
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A tree oozes sap and its bark is badly cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' looks like tree bark, but it is a dog's bark, whose second half is the piece that 'splitting' cuts open.
explanation.definitionFit: The willow with long drooping branches is a familiar ornamental tree beside water.

clue.text: New-fangled lip test for saliva

indicators.note: new-fangled suggests something made new, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A newfangled lip test checks a person's saliva.
explanation.definitionFit: Spittle is spit, the liquid in the mouth, so a direct synonym for saliva.

clue.text: Insects are often found trapped in this traffic light

definitions.text: Insects are often found trapped in this
definitions.meaning: fossil resin from ancient trees often holds preserved insects
the yellow light between red and green on traffic signals

explanation.definitionFit: Fossilised tree resin traps insects, and the middle signal colour shares its name.

clue.text: Buy tea blend offering quality that appeals

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tea blend is bought for its appealing quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty is attractiveness, the quality of pleasing the senses.

clue.text: More aggressively masculine slaughter

definitions.meaning: comparative of butch, meaning tough and macho

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative of butch; the other is the verb for killing savagely.

clue.text: Careful with money — three-fifty and no payment returned

indicators.note: no says the following letters are left out of the number spelt out
returned means the word for payment is read backwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: A frugal shopper spends three pounds fifty and gets no refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes EEF from FEE; take that run out of THREEFIFTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrifty means economical, using money sparingly and avoiding waste.

clue.text: Metropolitan Opera initially is in competition with films

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: New York's Met is competing with cinema for audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Movies is the everyday American word for films shown at the cinema.

clue.text: Time to follow fashions avoiding indecency

indicators.note: to follow puts the time letter after the fashions word

parts.note: modes are fashions or styles

explanation.surface: It's time to follow fashions that are not indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest dress is decorous and not revealing, so it avoids indecency.

clue.text: Start to tax one who receives the estate of those people

indicators.note: start to takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an heir inherits an estate

explanation.surface: Inheritance tax begins to bite on the person who inherits.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to them, of those people.

clue.text: Source of fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: Choosing whether to grow fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, where apples and pears come from.

clue.text: Initially coarse and unrefined?

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the next word

parts.note: rude here means rough or unpolished, as in rude huts

explanation.surface: Something that starts out rough and unpolished.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: crude means coarse and unrefined, as crude oil is unrefined.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude describes something in a raw natural state, rough and lacking polish.

clue.text: Rather ironically appearing regularly in dirty plays

indicators.note: appearing regularly in picks every other letter from the words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Smutty stage plays are viewed with a wry eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is understated and ironic, so speaking dryly means with quiet irony.

clue.text: Broadcasting band with great rate of repetition

parts.note: high means great, as in high hopes
frequency is how often something repeats

explanation.surface: A radio band with a strong beat repeats its tunes often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a range of radio wavelengths, HF (3-30 MHz).
explanation.definitionFit: HF is a named range of radio wavelengths used for shortwave broadcasting.

clue.text: Tall and thin? Wanting lots of food's not good

indicators.note: not says the letter for good is left out

parts.note: greedy means wanting lots of food

explanation.surface: A tall, skinny person craving lots of food is not good.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy describes someone slender like a reed, tall and thin.

clue.text: Treatment of those people about criminal charge

indicators.note: about says the pronoun goes around the charge

parts.note: they refers to those people
a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

explanation.surface: Those people get treatment for a criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: RAP is American slang for a criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is medical or psychological treatment for a condition.
